basicMistakes.where: Both logo slots at the far left and far right of the bug are blank light-grey squares with no team logo in them. The same happens in G-3, G-4, G-8 to G-16 and every operator-step frame.
After Next map the map line still reads 'KARTTA 3 · MIRAGE', with the same score and dots as before. No frame shows Next map doing anything.

missingActions: nextMap (the control exists, but no frame shows it changing anything)
otherProblems: Where logos do appear (G-5 to G-7), each sits on its own light-grey rounded tile. The pale crest almost disappears into the pale tile, which was the brief's warning about the pale yellow logo.
The 'OTTELU ALKAA' / 'ENNEN OTTELUA' phase chip is muted grey text on a grey chip and reads weak next to the other text.
With the long values, the left team name drops to a much smaller two-line size while the right name stays on one line. The two sides then look unequal in weight (G-5, G-11, G-14).
Map final straight after the Take changes nothing (G-33); it only works after Go live (G-67). That is a reasonable guard, but the frames never show Final on its own.
The live phase word is the English 'LIVE', while the other phase words are Finnish.
answer.reasons: This doesn't air as delivered. The overall build is sound: a dark glass bar centred at the top with team-colour underlines, clear score boxes, and long names that wrap or shrink cleanly without clipping, so it holds up over the busy ground. The logo slots are the problem. With the sample values they are empty grey squares, which reads as broken. With real crests, each logo sits on a pale tile of its own, and the pale yellow crest fades into it. I also have no frame where Next map changes the map or the dots, so I can't confirm the operator can advance the series.

basicMistakes.where: With the brief's own sample values the card shows only the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER tags and VS on two empty bands: no boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class appear. G-3 and G-12 to G-17 look the same.
After Select winner, neither corner changes. No winner is marked on either panel (same in G-18 to G-23).
Lock after Select only makes the centre divider flash for a moment (G-46 to G-49), then the card goes back to the empty default. No locked winner is ever shown.

Blue-corner name wrapped onto two lines. The acute accent on the second line's PHÁDRAIG runs into the 'EA' of SÚILLEABHÁIN on the line above because the line spacing is too tight. Also visible in G-5, G-10, G-11 and the G-59 crop.

missingActions: select (operator surface lists it, but no frame shows a winner being marked)
lock (only a brief flash of the divider; no locked state is shown)
clear (nothing visible to clear because no pick is ever shown)
otherProblems: Both gym logos sit on flat grey circular plates. The dark green-and-black logo comes out as a dark navy shield on grey, which looks muddy against the blue panel.
The two sides are inconsistent under stress: the red name stays on one line while the blue name wraps to two, so the sides' text blocks have different heights and spacing (G-4).
Long-side-only frames (G-8, G-10) drop the logos and the weight class entirely, and the other side stays an empty band holding only its tag.
The default state is two big empty coloured bands holding only small tags. They read as unfinished.
answer.reasons: This card wouldn't air. With the brief's own sample values it never shows the boxers, logos, records or weight class: every on-air and Take frame is just two empty coloured bands with corner tags. Selecting a winner changes nothing on screen, and locking only flashes the centre line for a moment. The core job of marking, locking and clearing a winner is never visible. Even in the long-value frames, where content does appear, the wrapped Irish name's accent runs into the line above, and the logos sit on grey circular plates.

otherProblems: The panel is a fixed width, so with short sample values about 200 px on its right side is empty. It reads as roomy rather than broken.
The thin timer rule at the bottom right is very faint and short. It could pass for a stray hairline rather than a progress bar.
The circular mask trims the top and bottom of the white shield avatar slightly (G-72). A viewer would barely notice it.
answer.reasons: This is a clean dark alert panel with an orange accent bar, a circular avatar and clear type: an orange tracked event label with the amount, a large white username and a lighter message. All of it reads well over the video, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut username fits on one line, and the long message wraps to two lines inside the panel, which grows to hold it. Nothing collides, clips or spills out. The white avatar stays clear on its dark circle. Hold, resume, replay and skip are all on the operator surface, and the frames show each one working: hold keeps the alert up past the timeout, skip clears it, and replay brings it back in again. The remaining nits are small, and a viewer would not see them as mistakes.

otherProblems: Suspense only dims the four nominees evenly, so the change on screen is small. It works but has little drama.
Behind each nominee is a nearly invisible dark card, and the cards differ in width with the name length, which makes their edges look slightly ragged.
When the long category title is shrunk to fit, the gap between the title and the gold rule grows (G-5), so the header spacing looks a little loose.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame, a gold eyebrow line, a strong white category title and a balanced stack of nominees, with film titles in gold mono. It stays readable over the video, light and busy backgrounds, because the board brings its own dark plate. The long category title and long names all fit inside the frame without clipping or overlap. Suspense dims the field and Reveal lifts the winner into a gold-lit card while the other three fade back. The winner is unmistakable, and both operator actions the brief needs are present. The take-in and take-out animations are clean, and the empty state shows only the title, which is fine. The remaining issues are small spacing and taste nits a viewer would hardly notice.

basicMistakes.where: Team A name wrapped onto two lines, 'KS CZĘSTOCHOWIANKA / CZĘSTOCHOWA': the lines are set so tight that the ogonek under the first-line Ę runs into the top of the second line
Top row name panel: same collision between the line-1 Ę ogonek and line 2 'CZĘSTOCHOWA'; also visible in G-8, G-9 and G-60 to G-64

otherProblems: When names are long, the type shrinks a different amount for each team (a small two-line name for A, a mid-size single line for B, against the larger default size), so the two rows don't match.
The shrunken names sit above the vertical centre of their panels (G-4, G-10), so top and bottom padding are uneven.
The left gutter kept for the serve dot is empty whenever no one is serving, which pushes the names in from the edge for no visible reason (G-2, G-30 to G-41).
The final look only drops the points column and moves the names to the left edge. There is no winner emphasis and no 'final' label, so it barely reads as a result.
End set was only pressed at 0:0, so the frames never show it awarding a set.
answer.reasons: I wouldn't put this on air as delivered. The strip itself is tidy: cream name panels, a black sets column and an orange points column, and it reads well on both grounds. Point A and point B move the serve dot properly, and Take and Out are clean. The problem is the brief's own requirement, long Polish names. The wrapped Team A name has such tight line spacing that the Ę ogonek runs into the line below. The long names also shrink to different sizes for each row and sit off-centre in their panels. The final state is barely distinguishable from the live state. As delivered, the long-name case doesn't hold up.

basicMistakes.where: Visitor crest (white and gold) in the left-hand disc of the bottom team row. It sits on a near-white ice-blue disc and almost disappears (see the G-87.png crop); the same happens on the light ground in G-5.jpg.

otherProblems: When no crest is supplied, the sample-value frames (G-2, G-3, G-16, G-22 and others) air two empty outlined circles beside the names. They are shapes holding nothing, and they read as missing artwork.
The goals-per-period strip never says which row belongs to which club. The only cue is a navy or gold rule under each row, and the navy rule sits tight under the home row's numbers.
The period strip's numbers and labels are small for television next to the large score and clock.
In the empty state (G-6, G-7) the clock shows a red 0:00 over a green underline, a clashing colour pair, and the period strip disappears.
The green bar under the clock never changes whether the clock is running or stopped, so it is just decoration under the time.
Resume play only removes the PŘESTÁVKA label; the clock does not restart (G-47, G-81).
answer.reasons: G-4 doesn't air as delivered. The overall layout is clean, and the long diacritic names wrap neatly into two lines without clipping. All five operator actions the brief needs are on the surface and visibly do something: the clock counts down and stops, and the PŘESTÁVKA and KONEC ZÁPASU labels appear. The problem is the crests. The white-and-gold visitor crest sits on a near-white disc and almost vanishes, which is exactly the case the brief warned about. When no crest is loaded, the board airs two empty rings. The period breakdown also doesn't say which row is which team, apart from thin coloured rules. A director would send it back for those fixes.

otherProblems: After the Session title update (G-41 to G-45), the names and gap figures settle at a smaller size and sit a few pixels high against the position chips. The board is still clean, but the type size is inconsistent with the other states.
The gap column is right-aligned well short of the DNF badge and the accent rule, which leaves an empty gutter of about 70 px on the right of the timed rows.
A flat grey strip under the panel reads as a hard offset shadow, and it shows most on the light ground (G-3, G-6, G-9).
In focus mode the dimmed DNF row is very dark grey on near-black. That is deliberate de-emphasis, but it is close to the edge of legibility.
answer.reasons: G should go on air as delivered. It is a clean, well-proportioned timing tower on the left of the frame, with a dark panel that stays readable over the video, light and busy grounds. Norwegian letters (Å, Ø, Æ) render correctly. In the stress frame the long double-barrelled name is cut short with a clean ellipsis inside its field, and the DNF rider is clearly marked with a dimmed row and an outlined badge. All three operator actions the brief needs work and the surface offers them. Focus brightens one row and dims the others, the whole-field view restores the board, and declaring the session final adds a lime "· FINAL" tag and recolours the position chips. None of the frames show overlaps, clipping or unreadable text. The only flaws are small: the type is smaller after a title update, and there is some uneven right-hand spacing in the gap column.

otherProblems: When answers in the same row differ in length, a one-line answer sits at the top of a box sized for two lines, while its letter chip is centred vertically (G-4/G-5/G-10, e.g. 'Lars Sonck', 'Hugo Alvar Henrik Aalto'). The text and letter end up slightly out of line.
In the judged state the wrong answers fade to a very pale grey-green on the near-white tiles (G-40/G-41). They can still be read on screen, but they may wash out on a projector.
Select on its own shows nothing on air (G-18–G-23). That fits the secret-pick flow, but in the select-lock-reveal mode the audience never sees a pick highlighted before the lock.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, balanced green-and-white board in the lower part of the frame. The question is bold and large, and the four answer tiles in a 2x2 grid get equal space. The long question and long answers wrap inside their fields on both grounds, with no clipping or collisions. Lock dims all four answers without giving away a letter, which is what the secret-pick flow needs. The correct answer then shows clearly as a solid green tile with white text, and the intro and outro animations are tidy. A designer would nit-pick that one-line answers are top-aligned against centred letter chips, and that the faded wrong answers are very light. Neither is enough to keep a school livestream graphic off air.

basicMistakes.where: With the sample values on air, both corner panels show only the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER tags. There are no boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class.
The settled Take, 10 s in, is still empty apart from the corner tags and the VS chip.
After Select winner the card is still empty and no winner is marked on either side.
After Select then Lock, the only change is that the centre rule gets longer. No locked winner is shown.
After updating the red name, the red side shows only the name and the blue panel stays empty.
Blue corner name wrapped onto two lines: the leading is so tight that the accent on 'PHÁDRAIG' runs into the line above, under 'SÚILLEABHÁIN'. Also visible in G-4.jpg and G-10.jpg.
With one side's long values, the other panel shows only its corner tag and is otherwise empty. Same in G-10.jpg.

missingActions: Select winner shows no visible winner state in any frame
Lock shows no visible locked state
Clear has nothing visible to undo
otherProblems: Both gym logos sit on grey circular plates of their own (G-4, G-65).
The dark green and black gym logo is shown in navy, not in its own colours.
The corner panels resize from frame to frame depending on what is filled in, so the card has no fixed layout.
Without a logo, the panel's text block shifts to sit just under the tag, and the panel looks unfinished.
answer.reasons: This card would not go on air. With the brief's own sample values it shows nothing but the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER tags and the VS chip, in every frame from the Take to Out. Select, Lock and Clear never produce a visible winner. Only the long stress values bring in names, records and logos, and even then the wrapped Irish name collides with itself and the logos sit on grey plates.

basicMistakes.where: Both logo slots, at the far left and far right of the team row, are blank light-grey squares with no logo in them. The same holds in every sample-value frame (G-3, G-4, G-28, G-46, G-68).
After Next map the board is unchanged: still KARTTA 3 · MIRAGE, the same map dots and the same phase pill. The step shows nothing on screen.

missingActions: nextMap: the button exists, but no frame shows the map number, map name or map dots changing.
otherProblems: When logos are present (G-5, G-78, G-79), each one sits on its own light-grey rounded plate instead of sitting directly on the glass bar.
Resume after Technical pause (G-74) puts the pill back to OTTELU ALKAA (pre-match) instead of LIVE, so a viewer would read the match as not started.
Map final straight after the Take (G-34) leaves the phase word unchanged. LOPPU only appears after Go live.
The long left team name drops to a smaller two-line setting while the long right name stays on one line and sits higher than the left name. The two sides are not set the same way.
The pre-match pill uses grey text on a grey pill, which reads weakly compared with the rest of the bar.
answer.reasons: The bar itself is well made: a dark glass panel centred at the top, with clear scores, a Bo dot row and accents split pale yellow and burgundy. Long names stay inside their fields on all three backgrounds. It still can't air. With the sample values, both logo slots are empty grey squares on screen, and when logos do load they sit on light plates of their own. Next map changes nothing visible, and Resume drops the phase back to pre-match instead of live. For a scorebug that runs a whole grand final, the logo and state problems are visible to viewers and would mislead them.

basicMistakes.where: Both corner panels with sample values show only the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER tags. No boxer names, gym logos, records or weight class appear, on either ground (G-3, G-16, G-17).
After Select winner, nothing changes on the board. No winner is marked in any select or lock frame (G-18–G-23, G-46–G-51), so the decision is never shown.
Lock it in makes no visible change, apart from the centre divider line stretching (G-46–G-51).
Blue-corner name wraps onto two lines with leading so tight that the acute accent on Á in 'PHÁDRAIG' runs into 'SÚILLEABHÁIN' on the line above (also in G-5, G-10, G-11 and crop G-59).
With only the red side filled, the blue panel is an empty box holding just its tag (and the reverse in G-10). The logos also disappear in these frames.

missingActions: select (no winner state is ever shown)
lock (no locked state is ever shown)
otherProblems: Each gym logo sits on a flat grey circular plate of its own (G-4, G-65, G-66), which looks like a placeholder.
The blue-corner logo reads as navy and black rather than the dark green and black the brief describes.
The record line is filled with placeholder text ('A long value that fills the line'), and the two sides' text blocks sit at different heights (G-4).
The panel height and layout change with the content, so the two-sided card looks unstable and unequal between states.
answer.reasons: With the brief's own sample values, the card shows only two corner tags and VS on panels that are otherwise empty. The boxers, gym logos, records and weight class never appear, and Select and Lock show no winner in any frame. Only the stress values fill the layout. Even then, the wrapped Irish name crashes its accent into the line above, and the logos sit on grey placeholder discs. A director would not put this on air.

otherProblems: With empty values the panel keeps showing an 'N' initial in the avatar even though there is no name, and most of the card is empty (G-8 to G-10). This is an edge case, and it is clean, not broken.
The progress hairline in the bottom right is very faint and barely reads as a timer (G-2, G-5).
With short values about 200 px of empty space is left on the right of the fixed-width panel (G-2). This is normal for left-aligned text and does not look broken.
The white shield avatar fills its circular mask almost to the edge, with only a little breathing room (G-72).
answer.reasons: This would air. It's a clean, dark top-right alert card with an orange accent bar and ringed avatar, and the hierarchy is clear: event label and amount, a bold name, then the message. The long umlaut username and the two-line message fit inside the panel with nothing clipped. The white avatar stays readable against the dark plate, and the card reads well over the video, light and busy grounds. Every action the brief needs works in the frames: the alert takes in and times out by itself, Hold keeps it up at 10 s, Resume lets it time out, Replay brings it back in, and Skip clears it at once. The Update and Out frames are clean too. I found nothing that blocks air, only small nits.

otherProblems: After the reveal the kicker still reads 'AND THE NOMINEES ARE'. There is no 'WINNER' label, so the gold-framed card alone tells viewers who won.
In the suspense state the nominees only dim to grey. It is a fairly flat way to build tension, though everything stays readable.
The faint dark plates behind each nominee change width with the name length. They are barely visible, but slightly uneven.
With the long category the title is set smaller, which leaves a larger gap above the gold rule than in the normal state.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. It sits on its own near-opaque panel, so the bright stage plate never hurts readability. None of the basic mistakes appear in any frame. The long names and the long category fit inside their fields without clipping, and the native-pixel crops confirm the glyphs are intact. Suspense and reveal both work: suspense dims the field, and the reveal isolates the winner in a gold-glow card while the others recede. The take and out animations are clean, and the empty state degrades to a tidy centred title. What remains are small finishing points: the kicker doesn't change after the reveal, and the backing plates are slightly uneven. A viewer wouldn't notice either, and neither would stop it going to air.

otherProblems: With the long category, the shrunken title leaves a slightly larger gap above the gold rule than in the sample layout. A viewer would barely notice it.
The nominee cards' faint dark backing plates change width from name to name. This is subtle and reads as intentional.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. It has a double gold frame, a gold kicker, a strong category title and four nominee cards with the film title in tracked gold caps. All text is large and readable on every ground, because the board's own near-black fill shields it from the bright stage behind. In the stress frames the long category and the long names and titles all fit inside the frame without clipping. Suspense dims all nominees evenly and they stay readable. Reveal lifts the winner into a gold-outlined card with a gold name, and the others drop back. Take, update and out animate cleanly. Both operator actions the brief needs are on the surface and work as shown.

otherProblems: The white shield avatar fills its circle edge to edge, and its top is slightly trimmed by the round mask (G-72, G-5).
In the empty-values frames (G-8 to G-10) the panel keeps its full width with only the 'DONATION' label in the top-left, and the avatar still shows an 'N' with no name next to it.
With sample values about 200 px of the panel's right side stays empty, and the faint countdown line at bottom right is barely visible.
answer.reasons: This is a clean top-right donation card. It has an orange accent bar, a ringed avatar, a monospace event and amount line, a bold name and a grey message, all readable on the video, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut username fits on one line, the long message wraps cleanly inside the panel, and the white avatar reads well on the dark circle. Hold keeps the alert on screen at 10 s. Resume, replay and skip all work, the label update and Out are clean, and no frame has text overlapping, clipped or escaping its panel. The remaining issues are small: a bit of empty width on the right, the mask trimming the avatar slightly, and a sparse empty state.

otherProblems: Both team logos sit on light-grey rounded square plates of their own at the ends of the bar (G-5, G-6, G-7, crops G-78, G-79).

With the brief's own sample values the logo plates are empty grey squares with nothing in them, reading as accidental blank blocks at both ends of the scorebug (G-2, G-21, G-27 and every sample-value frame).
The pale shield logo sits on a pale grey plate and nearly disappears into it (G-5, G-78).

The long-name sides get unequal treatment: Team A wraps to two lines at a smaller size, Team B stays on one line at a different size and sits higher than the centre line of its side (G-5, G-11, G-14).
The pre-match phase badge 'OTTELU ALKAA' / 'ENNEN OTTELUA' is grey text on a grey chip and reads weakly at a glance (G-2, G-5).
answer.reasons: The bar is clean and readable on every ground, and all five operator actions are on its surface. The phase word changes correctly to LIVE, TAUKO and LOPPU. It is held back by the logo treatment. Each logo sits on a grey square plate of its own, and with the brief's own values those plates show up as two empty grey tiles at the ends of the bar. That looks like a mistake. The pale logo also nearly disappears into its plate. With long names the two sides are set at different sizes and on different lines, which weakens the symmetry of a two-team board. Not airable as delivered.

otherProblems: In the brief's own sample frames (G-2, G-3 and every operator-step frame), both crest positions are empty light-blue circles with only a navy or gold outline beside 'Domácí'/'Hosté'. They read as unfilled placeholders, not crests. The same empty circles appear in G-6/G-7 and in the long-side frames G-8 to G-11.

The goals-per-period strip is a wide, mostly empty band. Its period numbers and per-period scores are very small for television, and the rows have no team labels: only a thin navy or gold rule under each row tells the viewer which team is which.
The green bar under the clock looks the same whether the clock is running or stopped (G-23 vs G-69), so it reads as decoration, not a status cue.
'KONEC ZÁPASU' in the final state (G-52/G-53) runs almost edge to edge in the clock column, leaving very little side padding.
answer.reasons: The panel is clean and the long Czech names wrap neatly within their field. Diacritics render correctly, nothing collides or is clipped, and Start, Stop, Interval, Resume and Final all work. Every action the brief needs is on the operator surface. However, with the brief's own sample values the board airs two empty outlined circles where the crests belong, which looks like a shape holding nothing rather than a crest. Together with the undersized, unlabelled period strip, a director would send this back for fixes rather than put it on air today.

otherProblems: With the sample values (G-2, G-3 and the step frames) the crest slots are empty pale rings with no crest inside. They look like placeholders whenever no crest is loaded.

The goals-per-period strip does not label which row belongs to which team. The only cue is a navy or gold rule under each row. The figures are small (about 18 px) and spread far apart across the wide strip.
With empty values (G-6, G-7) the clock reads 0:00 in red above the green accent bar, and the red and green look a little clumsy together. The away name slot is left blank.
The period headers change style between value sets: '1 2 3' with the sample values and '1. 2. 3.' with the long values.
KONEC ZÁPASU nearly fills the width of the clock column (G-52), leaving very little side padding.
answer.reasons: This is a clean white and ice-blue corner board, and it covers everything the brief asks for. Both crests appear when values are loaded, and both long Czech names wrap onto two lines without clipping and keep their diacritics. Every operator action changes the board visibly and correctly: the clock counts down, PŘESTÁVKA (interval) and KONEC ZÁPASU (final) both show, and Resume play returns to the normal state. The white-and-gold crest stays readable inside its gold ring, and contrast holds on both the dark and the light background. Text only looks cut during the Take wipe frames, which is part of the designed reveal. The weak points are the empty crest rings when no crest is loaded and a period breakdown that is small and has no team labels. A viewer would notice these, but they don't break the graphic.

basicMistakes.where: Select answer, settled at 10000 ms: all four answer boxes look exactly as they do before Select. No box shows a selected state, so the open select-lock-reveal flow gives the viewer nothing.
Reveal choice after Lock, settled at 10000 ms: all four answers stay evenly dimmed and no letter is highlighted. The captain's pick is never revealed in any frame.

otherProblems: Answers that fit on one line sit at the top of their box while the letter tile is vertically centred, leaving uneven empty space below (G-4/G-10, B/C/D in G-71–G-73).
On Reveal correct (G-41) the letter tile of the winning answer turns white with no border. On the white panel it fades into the background and looks like a gap in the row.
After Lock, the answer text is dimmed to a pale grey-green on pale green (G-29). This is weak contrast for a projector, and the losing answers after Reveal correct (G-41) are paler still.
answer.reasons: The board itself is clean and readable. It uses bold green and white, keeps two-line answers inside their boxes, and wraps the long question within its space. The judge step works: the correct answer turns solid green and the others dim. But the brief's core sequence breaks on screen. Select shows no selected state, and Reveal choice after Lock leaves every answer equally dimmed, so the captain's pick never appears in any frame. Single-line answers also sit top-aligned in boxes whose letters are centred, which makes those rows look unfinished.

basicMistakes.where: Select answer: the whole board looks exactly the same as before the step (compare G-17). No answer box is highlighted, so the team's pick never shows.
Reveal choice after Lock it in: all four answers stay equally dimmed and no letter is ever revealed as the captain's pick. Reveal choice alone (G-35) also changes nothing.

missingActions: select: no visible pick or highlight in any frame
revealChoice: no frame ever shows which letter the captain picked
otherProblems: Single-line answers sit at the top-left of their boxes while the letter badge is centred vertically. The lower half of each box is empty and the text does not line up with its letter (G-4, G-10: Lars Sonck, Aino Marsio-Aalto, Hugo Alvar Henrik Aalto).
On the correct-answer reveal (G-40), the letter tile turns white on the white panel. It loses its edge, so the badge looks detached from the green answer bar.
The dimmed answers after the reveal (G-40) and during the lock (G-28) are pale grey-green on near-white with low contrast. That is risky on a projector, which the brief calls out.
The question text wraps well short of the panel's right edge, leaving a large empty strip on the right.
answer.reasons: The base layout is clean: green and white, bold, readable type, and long questions and answers fit without clipping. The correct-answer reveal works. But the brief's main workflow depends on showing the captain's pick, and no frame ever does. Selecting an answer changes nothing on screen. The lock dims all four answers, and Reveal choice afterwards still names no letter, so the 'lock secretly, reveal pick, then reveal correct' sequence can't be run as delivered. On top of that, single-line answers float at the top of half-empty boxes, out of line with their letters. On the reveal, the white letter tile loses its edge against the white panel.

otherProblems: When the session title is updated to its long value (G-41 to G-45), the whole board re-renders with smaller type. Names and especially the gap times shrink, and the names sit slightly high against the position chips. The same long title taken fresh (G-5) keeps full-size rows, so the board visibly jumps mid-air.
In that updated state the subtitle stays in English ('GAP TO LEADER') under a Norwegian title.
The DNF row is inconsistent: a stray '–' appears in the gap column in the long-value frames (G-5 to G-7) but not in the sample frames.
The gap column ends at about x=724 while the DNF badge runs to the panel's inner edge at x=796, so the right edge of the rows is ragged. This is minor.
In focus mode the dimmed DNF row is very faint against the dark panel (G-20 to G-22). That is acceptable as deliberate de-emphasis, but it is close to the limit.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, well-proportioned timing tower: a dark panel down the left, lime position chips, a tidy accent rule under the header, and condensed names that keep their Norwegian letters (Å, Ø, Æ) intact. It reads on the video, light and busy grounds. The long double-barrelled name gets a clean ellipsis inside its field, and the DNF row is greyed with an outlined badge. Focus dims the other rows to bring one skier forward, the whole-field step restores the board, and the final step adds a lime 'FINAL' tag. The operator surface offers focus, clear and final. The worst flaw is that updating the title shrinks all the row type, which a director would want fixed, but everything stays readable and in bounds. No frame shows overlapping, clipped or unreadable text.

otherProblems: After the Session title update (G-41 to G-45), the names and gaps re-render at a smaller size and sit slightly high against the position chips. Viewers would see the board's text shrink mid-air.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10), the board stays full height: a large black panel with only the title and the rule, and nothing underneath.
The gap column ends about 70px short of the rule's right edge, so only the DNF badge reaches the right margin. The right-hand padding looks uneven.
In the focus state (G-21), the dimmed DNF row is very faint dark grey on black. It is still readable, but only just.
There is a flat grey strip under the panel's bottom edge. It reads more like a hard plinth than a designed shadow, which is most noticeable on the light ground (G-3).
answer.reasons: This is a clean, dark timing tower in the left third of the frame. Each row has a lime position chip, a condensed name and a gap, and the hierarchy is clear. Norwegian letters (Å, Ø, Æ) render properly. The longest stress name is cut cleanly with an ellipsis, the DNF row is greyed out with a DNF badge, and the panel stays readable over the light and busy grounds. Focus dims the other rows to bring one skier forward. Whole-field restores the board, and Final adds a lime "FINAL" tag and darkens every position chip except first place. The operator surface offers focus, clear and final. I found no overlaps, clipping or unreadable text in any frame. The remaining issues are small: the rows shrink after the session update, the empty state is a large blank box, and the right-hand padding is uneven. None of these stops the board going to air.

basicMistakes.where: Team A name field: the long name wraps to two lines with leading so tight that the ogonek under 'Ę' in 'KS CZĘSTOCHOWIANKA' drops into the caps of the second line 'CZĘSTOCHOWA'
Top row name plate, top-right strip: the line-1 'Ę' ogonek touches the 'CZĘSTOCHOWA' line below it. The same collision shows in G-5, G-8, G-9 and G-60 to G-64

otherProblems: When a long name arrives, the type shrinks a lot and the two rows end up in different sizes (a two-line micro name above a smaller one-line name, with 'GOŚCIE' still at full size in G-8). The strip looks inconsistent, and the small text is hard to read on a TV.
In the long frames, the row B name 'AZS UNIWERSYTET ŁÓDZKI' sits above the vertical centre of its plate.

The final look (G-46/G-47) moves the names to about 8px from the left border, so the left padding is cramped and a wide empty area is left before the set number. It also gives no 'final' label, so the viewer only sees the points column disappear.
No serve dot is shown in the sample on-air state (G-2), so the strip has no serving indicator until the first point is played.
answer.reasons: I would not put this on air as delivered. The basic strip works: cream name plates, a black sets box and orange points read cleanly in the corner. The point buttons add the point and move the serve dot, and new match, reopen and out all behave. The brief warns that the team names are long and Polish, and that is where it fails. The long name wraps with leading so tight that the 'Ę' ogonek runs into the next line. That is a text collision a viewer will see in the stress and update frames. The shrink-to-fit also leaves the two rows in clearly different type sizes, and in the final look the names are pushed almost against the left border.

basicMistakes.where: Top row, two-line name 'KS CZĘSTOCHOWIANKA / CZĘSTOCHOWA': the lines are set so tightly that the ogonek under the first line's Ę drops onto the cap tops of 'ĘS' in the second line (also visible in G-5, G-8, G-60–G-64 and the G-70 crop)

otherProblems: The type size changes from row to row: a wrapped or long name shrinks to a much smaller size than 'GOSPODARZE' or 'GOŚCIE' in the other row (G-4, G-10), so the two teams get unequal visual weight.
The two-line name block and the shrunk single-line 'AZS UNIWERSYTET ŁÓDZKI' sit above the row's vertical centre and do not line up with the large score digits.
The final look (G-46/47) only drops the points column. It has no 'FINAL' or 'KONIEC' label, so viewers can't tell it from a live score.
In the final look the names move hard against the left border with about 10 px of padding, leaving a wide empty cream area to their right. The padding is badly uneven compared with the live state.
The sets and points columns carry no labels at all, so in a compact strip the two numbers are hard to tell apart.
answer.reasons: The live strip itself is clean: the cream name panels, black sets cell and orange points cell read well on both grounds, and the serve dot follows the point buttons correctly. Undo, end-set and out all behave. The stress names are what keep it off air. The long Polish club name wraps into two cramped lines where the first line's Ę ogonek runs into the second line, and long names drop to a visibly smaller size than the other team's. The final look is also weak: it carries no 'final' marker and pushes the names against the left edge. A director wouldn't take this as delivered for a show whose names are long and full of Polish letters.
